definitions.explanation: A harmful event or trouble that brings suffering. More literary and weighty than everyday words for trouble, often used in proverbs and set phrases.

examples.japanese: {災|わざわ}い⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{招|まね}く→招く：02425_maneku⟧。

examples.english: They say the mouth is the source of misfortune.

examples.japanese: ⟦{不注意|ふちゅうい}→不注意：15111_fuchuui⟧な⟦{一言|ひとこと}→一言：03708_hitokoto⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{思|おも}わぬ→思う：00492_omou⟧{災|わざわ}い⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{招|まね}く→招く：02425_maneku⟧こと⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: A careless remark can sometimes invite unexpected trouble.

notes:
A weighty, somewhat literary word for harm or misfortune that befalls someone. Common in proverbs and set expressions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {災|わざわ}い⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{招|まね}く→招く：02425_maneku⟧: to invite disaster
- ⟦{口|くち}→口：00560_kuchi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{災|わざわ}い⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{元|もと}→元：03878_moto⟧: careless words bring trouble (proverb)
- {災|わざわ}い⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{転|てん}じて{福|ふく}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{為|な}す→為す：03915_nasu⟧: to turn misfortune into fortune (proverb)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{災害|さいがい}→災害：09636_saigai⟧: disaster — refers to large-scale natural or accidental disasters; {災|わざわ}い is broader and often about personal misfortune
